title: Roman to Integer
description:
Roman numerals use seven symbols: `I`=1, `V`=5, `X`=10, `L`=50, `C`=100, `D`=500, `M`=1000. Symbols are normally written from largest to smallest and added together, but six subtractive pairs exist: `IV`=4, `IX`=9, `XL`=40, `XC`=90, `CD`=400, `CM`=900, where a smaller symbol placed before a larger one is subtracted.

Given a valid Roman numeral `s`, return its integer value.
constraints: s contains only the characters I, V, X, L, C, D, M
s is a valid Roman numeral in the range [1, 3999]
hints: Map each symbol to its value and sum them. Where does that go wrong?
A symbol is subtracted exactly when the symbol to its right is larger. Compare each value with its right neighbour.
Scanning right to left, keep the previous value: add the current value if it is >= previous, subtract otherwise.
approach:
**Key insight: a symbol is subtracted if and only if a bigger symbol follows it.** That single rule covers all six subtractive pairs, so you never need to special-case `IV`, `IX`, and so on. Walk the string once, look at the right neighbour, and add or subtract.

An equivalent formulation scans right to left and tracks the previous (right-hand) value: add when the current value is at least the previous, subtract when it is smaller. Both are O(n) with a 7-entry table.

**Common mistakes:** hard-coding the two-character pairs and then skipping an index incorrectly; using a list of pairs sorted by length and doing repeated `startswith`, which is correct but noisy; forgetting the last character has no right neighbour.

**Interview follow-ups:** Validate the numeral as well as parse it (no more than three repeats of I/X/C/M, V/L/D never repeated, only the six legal subtractive pairs). Write the inverse (`integer-to-roman`). Extend to numbers above 3999 using the overline notation (multiply by 1000), which breaks the fixed symbol table.
